_meta.description: Brand-level RTSP URL templates for IP cameras, each verified against the manufacturer's own documentation.
_meta.methodology: StrixCamDB is used ONLY as a lead source; every path here is independently re-verified against the manufacturer's official docs (manual / API / KB), so each record is independently sourced and CC0-clean, with Strix credited as the discovery source (strix_lead). Leads that could not be confirmed officially are recorded under unverified_leads and never published as fact.

templates.source: 2N wiki — Starting manual for integration with 2N IP Intercoms: https://wiki.2n.com/faqint/en/startovaci-manual-pro-integraci-s-2n-ip-interkomy-104862445.html

brands.notes: 2N IP intercoms expose per-codec RTSP paths, not a main/sub hierarchy. Official docs list four paths: / (uses configured profile), /h264_stream (H.264), /mpeg4_stream (MPEG-4), /mjpeg_stream (MJPEG). No sub-stream or channel-indexed URL is documented. RTSP is limited to 4 parallel connections. An Enhanced Video licence (Part No. 9137906) is required to enable streaming on older firmware; newer Helios models include it. 2N is now an Axis subsidiary. Port 554 is the RTSP default; docs do not specify a non-standard port.

brands.notes: 3S Vision (brand of 3S System Tech. Inc. / 3S Pocketnet Technology Inc., Taiwan; site 3svision.com.tw / 3svision.us). Official RTSP URI syntax is documented in the N3072 user manual: rtsp://<ip>:554/cam<N>/<codec>-<idx>, default port 554, where cam<N> selects the channel (N=1..4; single cameras use cam1, 4-channel video servers use cam1..cam4) and the trailing -1 = main stream, -2 = sub stream. Confirmed variants: /cam1/h264-1 (main), /cam1/h264-2 (sub), plus /cam1/3gpp for mobile. Firmware release notes (3svision.com.tw, 2013-2014) confirm ONVIF Profile S support and H.264 Baseline/Main/High profiles. The ONVIF-media paths (/cam1/onvif-h264[-1]) reported by third-party aggregators are ONVIF-service URIs consistent with this scheme but not printed verbatim in the official manual, and the /mpeg4 codec paths, while structurally valid, likewise are not shown verbatim in the manual seen — all left under unverified_leads.

brands.notes: 3xLOGIC is a US professional surveillance brand (VISIX IP camera line, integrates with 3xLOGIC VIGIL Server/VMS). The only literal RTSP URL printed in an official 3xLOGIC document is the auto-set main-stream path in the VISIX VX-2A-B-IWD user manual: rtsp://[ip]/ch0_unicasy_firststream — a typo for the well-known generic 'ch0_unicast_firststream' first-stream path (port 554). Stream type is selectable (MPEG4/JPEG/H264). The sub/second stream follows the same ch0_unicast_secondstream convention but is NOT printed literally in an official doc, so it is left verified:false. VISIX cameras are also ONVIF Profile S compliant (VIGIL Server can auto-detect via ONVIF Device Manager), so the RTSP URI can alternatively be obtained via ONVIF GetStreamUri. All of the StrixCamDB leads (ch0_0.h264, video.h264, stream0, live/mpeg4, Hikvision /Streaming/Channels/1, Dahua /cam/realmonitor) are cross-brand contamination and none match the official 3xLOGIC path — excluded.

brands.notes: ABUS (ABUS Security-Center GmbH, Affing, Germany) runs its own native IP camera firmware platform across the TVIP and IPCB/IPCS series. Official ABUS user manuals (TVIP62000, TVIP11502, TVIP21502 — confirmed via ManualsLib) document three RTSP path variants on the native platform: /h264 (H.264), /mpeg4 (MPEG-4), /mjpeg (MJPEG), all on port 554 with credentials in the URL (rtsp://{user}:{pass}@{ip}:554/<codec>). The older TVIP41550 uses a configurable access-name scheme rather than fixed paths. The heavily-represented Hikvision /Streaming/Channels/101 path appears only in community aggregators for ABUS and is not confirmed by any official ABUS documentation reviewed — it is treated as cross-brand lead contamination. ABUS may sell some Hikvision-OEM models (community sources mention a 'CF3' model), but no official ABUS document was found confirming Hikvision RTSP paths for ABUS-branded hardware. The /mjpeg path is a valid third stream option not listed as a separate template here since the spec focuses on main/sub; integrators should use /mjpeg for MJPEG access.

brands.notes: ACTi cameras expose RTSP streams at /stream<N> (1-based: /stream1 = main, /stream2 = sub, up to /stream4 on some models). The RTSP access name is user-configurable in the camera web UI (Streaming > RTSP > Access Name); /stream1 is the typical factory default observed in ACTi's own VLC guide. Default RTSP port is 554 per the current firmware manual. Port 7070 documented in the older ACTi Streaming Explorer tool (2011) is ACTi's proprietary SDK streaming protocol port — not standard RTSP. Cameras supporting up to 4 streams use /stream1–/stream4. ACTi is a Taiwanese manufacturer (acti.com), not an OEM of Dahua or Hikvision.

brands.notes: ADT-branded IP cameras sold under the ADT Pulse program (OC810, OC835, OC845, RC8010, RC8021, RC8025B, RC8325, NV412A, etc.) are manufactured by Sercomm Corporation, confirmed by FCC filings (FCC ID P27OC835 by Sercomm) and Amazon product listings. The Sercomm platform exposes two RTSP endpoints: /img/video.sav (video only) and /img/media.sav (video + audio); the latter is the more complete stream. Both share RTSP port 554 (configurable). /img/audio.sav (audio only) and /img/video.mjpeg (MJPEG HTTP) also exist per Sercomm docs but are not primary RTSP video streams. ADT does not appear to publish its own RTSP integration guide — the Sercomm OEM firmware is the authoritative reference for these paths. brands.notes: Advidia is a Panasonic i-PRO reseller brand whose cameras are OEM'd, and the OEM has changed across generations — so there are TWO documented RTSP families. (1) Current M-series (M-24-FW-T, M-26-FW, M-29-FW, M-46-FW, M-49-FW, M-400-P, etc.) = Uniview (UNV) OEM: the official i-PRO Advidia 2MP/4MP user manuals show the Uniview Web-UI, and Uniview's official RTSP doc gives /media/video1 (main), /media/video2 (sub), /media/video3 (third), port 554. (2) Legacy A-series and some VP-series (A-34W, A-37FW, A-47, VP-16-V2) = Hikvision OEM: standard Hikvision /Streaming/Channels/<ch><stream> — 101 main, 102 sub, 103 third; published on OEM-lineage basis (this also matches the dominant leads). No single official Advidia document prints a literal RTSP URL string (i-PRO's NVR manual explicitly says to 'contact the camera manufacturer for the resource path'), so the literal paths come from the confirmed OEMs' own docs. Also note some very old Advidia/VP units (Dahua-based /cam/realmonitor) exist in leads but were NOT confirmed and are excluded as cross-brand contamination. All families default to RTSP port 554; ONVIF is supported for auto-discovery on all.

RTSP/RTSPS is disabled by default and must be enabled PER CAMERA in the Protect UI (Cameras > Select Camera > Manage > RTSP, or UniFi Devices > [camera] > Settings > Advanced). An unencrypted variant rtsp://{console-ip}:7447/{streamToken} is also available on some firmware (port 7447). The {streamToken} is a random ~16-char token, unique per camera and non-guessable — hence there is no shareable static template beyond the token form. Scope: Ubiquiti UniFi Protect cameras served via a Protect console; the separate 'ubiquiti' brand entry covers Ubiquiti's non-Protect/legacy UniFi Video (airVision) cameras.
